messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: node-notready in cluster=prod-usw, node=infer-node-17 (10.12.17.220). Affected pods: inference-pool-usw-*.  Service impact: increased 5xxs and pod restarts. Pager severity: P2. First seen: 2026-03-15T02:12:01Z

alice (oncall): acked. I'm taking it. pulling logs and checking node health.

alice (oncall): quick health checks:
```
kubectl get nodes infer-node-17 -o wide
NAME            STATUS     ROLES    AGE   VERSION
infer-node-17   NotReady   <none>   47d   v1.28.x
```

ben (sre): any kubelet restarts in kube-system? can you `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` and check kubelet/journal?

alice (oncall): grabbing kubelet logs now. saw multiple `kubelet: CRITICAL: kubelet restarted` events every ~90s. tailing journal: 
```
Mar 15 02:10:12 infer-node-17 kubelet[1234]: E0325 02:10:12.123456 kubelet_node_status.go:120] Node conditions: Kubelet stopped heartbeat
Mar 15 02:10:13 infer-node-17 kernel: [12345.678901] Out of memory: Kill process 9876 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
Mar 15 02:10:13 infer-node-17 nvrm: NVRM: GPU 0000:3b:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

carlos (infra): NVRM messages + OOM suggests either GPU driver crash or kernel OOM due to memory pressure. check `dmesg` and `nvidia-smi -q` if node still reachable.

alice (oncall): node is flaky; `kubectl get node` shows NotReady intermittently. `nvidia-smi` times out when it answers. Pod logs for a model runtime show cuda OOMs: 
```
2026-03-15T02:09:58Z model-runtime[pid]: ERROR: CUDA error: out of memory when allocating 512MB
2026-03-15T02:10:00Z model-runtime[pid]: ERROR: unloading due to fatal GPU error: GPU has fallen off the bus
```

ben (sre): ok, mitigation plan: cordon + drain this node, accelerate failover of inference pods to other healthy nodes, and temporarily reduce concurrency/batch size on the pool to reduce mem pressure. Also enable routing fallback to infer-pool-eu or dedicated-capacity for critical customers.

alice (oncall): executing now.
```
kubectl cordon infer-node-17
kubectl drain infer-node-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
```

support-bot: Note: draining pods will trigger rescheduling; pods may pull capacity in other AZs. Watch for cross-AZ latency increase.

jordan (se): heads up—we have two enterprise customers (acme-corp, finlytics) on routing A/B to this pool. I'm messaging account owners and will post an advisory.

anna (cs): ON IT. sending internal note to acct teams and prepped a customer message: "We are experiencing degraded inference throughput in US-West. We have routed requests away from affected nodes; some increased latency and errors may persist while we complete node recovery. We'll update in 30 minutes."

alice (oncall): drain completed, most inference pods rescheduled to other nodes. however capacity in usw is close to saturated; autoscaler is pending additional node provisioning (GCP). scaling up now: 
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment infer-pool-usw --replicas=18
```

ben (sre): while nodes spin up, reduce pool concurrency and batching to lower per-pod memory. Applying a transient config: 
```
PATCH /api/configs/infer-pool/usw
{
  "max_concurrency": 2,
  "batch_size": 8
}
```

alice (oncall): applied. monitoring error rates and 5xxs. Metrics: 5xx spikes from 0.3% -> 6.1% at peak, now down to ~1.8% after actions. Latency p95 increased ~120ms due to cross-node scheduling.

carlos (infra): I pushed a kernel-driver rollback on the suspicious image family on a canary host (driver v525 -> v515) and suggested node imaging for infer-node-17 if it returns. Might be recent driver update causing instability.

ben (sre): good call. also looking at kube-proxy/node heartbeat patterns — this looks like memory leak in runtime container causing kernel to OOM and then kubelet restart loop. We should mark node for reprovision.

alice (oncall): marking node for reprovision and opening a ticket to rebuild. `node-alloc` now shows reduced capacity, but failover is holding.

support-bot: Customer impact summary (automated): 18k requests in last 30m to infer-pool-usw; 9% error rate at peak affecting 24 customers, 3 customers saw >25% error rate. Identified customers: acme-corp, finlytics, devtools-inc. Suggested outreach: CS+AE immediate for top 3.

jordan (se): sent messages to AEs for acme-corp and finlytics. acme response: "We're seeing job failures in batch integrations—anything we should change client side?" I recommended retry/backoff and routing to eu as temporary.

anna (cs): customers contacted. acme asked for ETA. I'm saying 60-90 minutes while we reprovision and monitor.

ben (sre): post-mortem action items (short):
- reprovision infer-node-17 (carlos)
- investigate driver versions across fleet and roll back if correlated (ben + infra)
- add memory/cuda OOM alerts per-node earlier (alice + monitoring)
- run chaos test for GPU driver upgrades in staging (sre + eng-runtime)

carlos (infra): creating infra ticket INFRA-5421 to reprovision and pin nodes. Will include kernel and nvidia driver versions.

alice (oncall): preparing handoff to next oncall in 30m. Current state summary for handoff: 
- root cause: suspected GPU driver/kernel interaction causing CUDA errors -> container OOM -> kubelet restarts -> node NotReady
- mitigation performed: cordon+drain, reduced concurrency/batch, scaled replicas, routed critical customers to fallback, contacted customers
- outstanding: reprovision infer-node-17, fleet driver audit, monitor error rates until <0.5% for 1 hour

ben (sre): agree. I'm staying on until reprovision ticket is created. tagging @sre-lead for visibility.

jordan (se): thanks all. will follow up with account execs after next metrics check.

alice (oncall): handing off to ben in 30. If error rate creeps back above 2% or kubelet flaps reappear, please escalate immediately.

ben (sre): taking the handoff. summary accepted. I'll own the ticket and keep this thread updated. :thumbsup: 

support-bot: Incident severity remains P2. Next update scheduled in 20 minutes or on changes.

anna (cs): leaving a note in the customer channel: "We're continuing to route traffic and monitor. We'll update within the hour." :pray: 

ben (sre): bumping after 25m: node reprovision started (INFRA-5421). autoscaler added 3 instances; error rate steady at 0.9%. continuing to watch logs and GPU metrics.

alice (oncall): thanks — handoff complete.

ben (sre): closing loop later with postmortem and timeline. tagging eng-runtime for root-cause deep dive on driver interactions. :eyes:
